text:
Rep. Nunn recognized for responding to over 340,000 constituent messages in Iowa
Rep. Zach Nunn received national recognition on July 21 for his office's efforts in answering more than 340,000 messages from Iowans since the beginning of the year.
“When an Iowan picks up the phone or writes to their representative, they deserve to know a real person is listening and working to get them an answer,” said Rep. Nunn. “Whether it’s a veteran trying to access VA benefits they’ve earned, a senior waiting on their Social Security check, or a family wanting their voice heard on an issue before Congress, serving Iowans is the job. I’m honored by this recognition, but the greatest reward is hearing from an Iowan who finally got an answer or solved a problem with our office’s help.”
Nunn's office reported responding to nearly 342,000 letters, emails, phone calls and other inquiries—an increase of 32 percent over the same period last year and a 56 percent increase compared to 2023. The Congressional Management Foundation’s Democracy Awards recognized these efforts as part of its program highlighting excellence in congressional offices' day-to-day operations.
Winners of the Democracy Awards are selected by an independent panel of judges from more than 150 applications submitted by congressional offices across the country.
Nunn represented Iowa's Third Congressional District covering 21 counties in central and southern Iowa and operated his office out of Des Moines while offering constituent assistance with federal agencies, according to the official website. He served on both the House Financial Services Committee and House Agriculture Committee while prioritizing pragmatic bipartisan policies focused on economic growth, support for agriculture, government accountability, national security and family support.
